title: Approximation of affine morphisms at a finite stage
explicit_hypotheses: I is a directed indexing set, 0\in I, and (S_i)_{i\in I} is an inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms.
S=\varprojlim_{i\in I}S_i.
f_0:X_0\to Y_0 is a morphism of schemes over S_0.
S_0, X_0, Y_0 are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
For every i\ge 0, f_i:X_i\to Y_i is obtained from f_0 by base change along S_i\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is the corresponding base change of f_0 along S\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is affine.
conclusion_claims: There exists i\ge 0 such that f_i:X_i\to Y_i is affine.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) be a directed inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit \(S=\varprojlim_i S_i\). Fix \(0\in I\) and a morphism of \(S_0\)-schemes \(f_0:X_0\to Y_0\) with \(S_0,X_0,Y_0\) quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each \(i\ge 0\), let \(f_i:X_i\to Y_i\) be the base change of \(f_0\) to \(S_i\), and let \(f:X\to Y\) be its base change to \(S\). If \(f\) is affine, then there exists \(i\ge 0\) such that \(f_i\) is affine.
